writeup: TIC 348762141 is a candidate eclipsing binary star detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The system shows a primary eclipse with 12.09% dimming and a secondary eclipse detected at 9.9 sigma significance. The initial analysis suggested an orbital period of 17.9384 days, but a significant data quality flag indicates that alternating eclipses differ substantially in depth - a signature suggesting the true period is actually double this value, at 35.876786 days. Pixel-level image analysis confirms the signal originates from the target location, with a peak signal-to-noise of 49.4, though a 1.5 arcsecond centroid offset was noted. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, suggesting it has not been previously identified in this way.
